questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I have lived in Italy before, but that was for work, so I wanted to go back and experience the country in an academic setting, by attending university and experience what that would be like. It was important to me that I could choose courses that were still relevant to my direction of studies (Asian Studies) in Copenhagen, to make my electives work in line with other courses I have taken in Denmark and Japan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Overall I have been very pleased with the study abroad experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. Websites both of University of Copenhagen and University of Milan were easy to use regarding finding information, and the International Office/Study Abroad offices both places were very good at supporting me every step with providing the guidance and information that I needed.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There wasn't much, but this was due to Covid. However, the support online from the International Office was always there, the student cards could be picked up in an easy way, and the screens at the university and the website guided me to find classrooms, updated timetables etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, it was a bit expensive, but finding it was not too difficult. I found my room in an apartment with two others at the website HousingAnywhere.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It gives a nice freedom to have maybe a bigger or more privat space, I had my own bathroom for instance, which was really nice, but that also meant that the price was more expensive. I had a nice room, but it was too expensive for my budget in reality, so I had to spend additional money myself, so I would definitely recommend to others finding cheaper accomodation, so there is more room in the budget for other stuff, taking little trips on weekends etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: At least off campus, I was very satisfied with my place, nice and clean, and the only issue really was the price, which was in the expensive end.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything worked well, and if I had a doubt or question, I could easily reach out to the International Office.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Registration was partly through Mobility Online with upload of various documents. Upon arrival I confirmed the courses I wanted to follow, and was quickly able to access the courses' different forums on Ariel, to search for readings etc. After a while, I received my student card with my Erasmus Student number.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Through email and online, help was provided quickly and efficiently. Staff at the university campus itself was also very helpful in case I had additional doubts or questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesful. After the first two classes I had followed, I had two ones, where one of them I confirmed and continued with, and the other I wanted to change and replace with another. Also this process was very easy, and the host university helped me with information on how to attend the new class, so I could search for an updated pre-approval at my home university.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No other advice other than it is very easy and accessible. If in doubt, my experience was, that writing an email will clarify any question about the process.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic programme was very good, the content varied and the professors very skilled and interesting to follow during class.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses I took were mainly for MA students, but I didn't experience problems with following the courses. Some of them required a bit of basis pre-knowledge, but fortunately I had had similar contents during other courses in either Denmark or Japan.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style is similar. I think it was a nice combination of academic but creative writing, and more standard memorizing the teaching sort of style.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
I followed four courses during the semester, two in one trimester and two in another one.
First I had International Relations and Language in Politics, secondly I followed Global Geopolitics and International Relations of East Asia.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I think it very much depends on the person's own personal interest. I liked all of the above mentioned courses, because they involve my interest in politics, language and rhetoric, international relations and global affairs etc.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The rent was higher than what I expected to pay when I first thought of going on exchange. I also had a security deposit and service fee to pay when I moved in. I had quite a big problem with money because of my high rent, but was unable to find something else to live in, and so I had to spent some of my own, and borrow some additional money.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Rent was more expensive, transportation was less expensive, the travel card I had was just 300 a month for the metro, tram and busses all over Milan. Books and readings could be found online mostly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think there were several well-functioning activities, but I unfortunately didn't attend any clubs or sporting activities, due to a lack of time.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were many social and cultural activities and trips arranged for students, really a wide variety of options.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Going to some of the social events organised for the Erasmus by students of the host university or other exchange students, they really aim to create a social climate, and organising trips for the students to see more of Italy, and meet new people while on exchange.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Definitely go to see some of the near by places such as Lake Como, it's beautiful, and I was there several times. With perhaps some more time on weekends I would recommend going to other big cities such as Rome or Venice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: To me it was very easy. I have lived in Italy before and know the culture and the language, but it was also nice to experience the regional differences there are in Italy. I just to live south of Rome, which was partly why I also wanted to go to Milan, to experience a different part of Italy in a new setting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to the Erasmus meetings or events, I didn't attend many actually, but just attending a few made me meet people and speak to people in the local environment. Also in class it can be a good idea to say hi to the local students or maybe sometimes ask them a question you have for something regarding a course or something, instead of always writing an email to a professor or the office, in that way you help each other and start talking with the other students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not really many, I think Italy is a wonderful and in many ways easy accessible culture. Of course the language can be difficult when you don't know some basics, so learning some of the local language is always a good idea. The Erasmus program offered language courses based on a language placement test, which was also nice to have the possibility to attend.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Every part really. The food, the language, the beauty of the culture. The social factor, it was easy to speak to people, as has also been my previous experience in Italy.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy the city and also get outside the city to see some of the beautiful places around Milan. Learn some Italian, even if just 'ciao', it is a very nice way to engage with your local community also, and makes you feel more at home. Ask for help, send an email to the International Office or ask other students if you are in doubt of something. Or say hi to someone and ask what courses they attend or something. It's always nice to feel like a part of something, and usually this is how conversations, encounters and friendships start.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: None other than keep yourself updated on the email of both your host and home university, to make sure you know what the next step of the exchange is and so on.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To be in Italy in a study setting and to see more of the country. It became of course very warm in the late spring and summer months, which can be hard to concentrate in, but I actually think it worked out well as it is a very nice place to attend university  in general, and I was very pleased with the experience.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The rent. I would definitely recommend everyone to find a place where it is not too expensive if possible, apply for student housing in time, so that there is some more financial freedom to do stuff and not worry too much about economics every month.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Go on exchange. I have done it in both Japan and Italy now, and I have loved both. It can be a challenge, but an absolutely amazing opportunity to see new places and meet new people, and I have never regretted for a minute that I decided to travel and study abroad.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
